what_changed: src/sec10k/eval_adapter.py: new `meta_field` check type — `item_field`'s counterpart for the contract's normative `meta` keys, asserting one by value.

src/sec10k/eval_adapter.py::envelope_shape: recomputes the contract's own definition of coverage (span-carrying chars / normalized chars, 4 dp) from the items the SAME envelope publishes, and refuses any envelope whose published `meta.coverage` disagrees. [CORRECTED under PR #57 R4: this bullet originally went on to call this 'the root-cause binding' for the finding's second-order point, on the grounds that extract.py's and validate.py's two calls to coverage() were now pinned by their AGREEMENT. That was FALSE. The check judges the publisher only; validate.py's `cov = coverage(text, items)` is read by no committed case. (PR #57 R5: it is now read by validate._demo, a CI-run self-check — still not by an eval case, but no longer by nothing.) What this bullet actually delivers is the binding of the PUBLISHED figure to the contract definition — which is real, and which R4 left closed — and nothing more.]

resolutions.red_evidence: The reviewer's own mutant (`meta["coverage"] = 1.0`) applied verbatim at ec2d0a5: first reproduced the finding (invariant 69/69 = 1.000, fast 132/132 = 1.000 while every document publishes coverage 1.0), then the pins were added against the STILL-MUTATED tree and went red for the right reason — `meta.coverage 1.0 != 0.0303` and `!= 0.982`, with 24 cases red across the full suites (invariant 62/69 = 0.899, fast 108/132 = 0.818). Mutant reverted: all green.
resolutions.note: [CORRECTED under PR #57 R4 — the original text of this field was: 'One producer was considered and NOT taken. Collapsing extract.py and validate.py onto a single computed value is a behaviour-neutral refactor whose blast radius would still have to be re-measured, and it would not fix the defect — a single producer can still publish a figure no case ever reads. Pinning the agreement is the smaller and the stronger change. Recorded in ADR-034 s.f1.' Its last clause was false: no agreement is pinned. The two call sites can still silently diverge, which is exactly the defect class R1 raised. The correct statement is that the PUBLICATION is bound to the contract definition and the second call site's agreement is UNPINNED; that gap is now carried as a debt row in tasks/TODO.md (Origin: PR #57 R4), and the disposition is recorded in tasks/reviews/pr57-r2-resolution.json.] [FURTHER CORRECTED under PR #57 R5: the debt row named above has been DELETED and no longer exists. The second call site is now pinned in its own right — `validate._demo` asserts that an IBR-only span over the 10,018-char stub produces a `low_item_coverage` message reading 0.2%, which the round-2 mutant turns into 0.0% (tasks/reviews/pr57-r3-red.txt). Their AGREEMENT is still not pinned; each is pinned to a literal instead, which makes a divergence between them red. The cost claim this field carried — that binding the second call site required a validate() signature change — was false and is superseded; see tasks/reviews/pr57-r3-resolution.json.]
resolutions.kept_two_call_sites_note: Kept, and their agreement is NOT pinned — see the corrected `note`. Added under PR #57 R4 so this field cannot be read as a claim of coverage. [PR #57 R5: still kept, still no agreement pin, but each call site now carries its OWN literal pin — the publisher via envelope_shape + two meta_field checks, the thresholder via validate._demo's 0.2% assertion — so the two cannot diverge silently.]

corrections.why_note: A second correction entry follows, under PR #57 R5.
corrections.why: This artifact asserted that extract.py's and validate.py's two calls to coverage() were pinned by their agreement. The round-2 reviewer falsified it: mutating validate.py's call to count `extracted` spans only leaves invariant 69/69 and fast 132/132 green while 24 of the 39 span-bearing dev fixtures threshold a different number from the one they publish. Corrected in place rather than silently, because a committed resolution artifact is read as verified-correct — the same reason ADR-034 s.f1 carries its own correction note.

The R4 correction above pointed at a debt row that no longer exists. R5 showed the deferral's cost claim was false — binding validate.py's call site costs two lines in validate._demo, not a signature change — so the pin was taken and the debt row deleted. These fields are annotated in place so nothing here still cites the deleted row or the superseded cost. Disposition: tasks/reviews/pr57-r3-resolution.json.
